analysis.title: GS Miller - [GSX] Global Reflections 9 Oct 2026
key_insights: Desk takeaway from a week of macro client meetings: the pace of the rate rise matters, and the ~68bps rise since August-end is concerning. Had the same move taken six months it would have been perceived differently.
Oil and rates had been moving in line with one another but stopped, which has unsettled many clients. The de-escalation scenario is described as impossible to predict.
The Midterms are perceived as a clearing event for AI Power. The AI vs ex-AI equity spread widened to a record 10pp in 5 weeks until this week.

The desk likes adding non-AI exposure despite the lack of clarity on geopolitics. Favorite implementations are Consumer Experiences, Healthcare and the SPXXAI Index. SPXXAI Nov 103% calls cost 0.75% (~13v, 25d).

Brazil: the first-round election outcome strengthened expectations for lower local interest rates, with softer growth, a firmer BRL and improved fiscal sentiment at the long end. The desk favors Brazil Rate Sensitive Stocks (GSBZRATE). Historically the basket returned roughly three times the Ibovespa in prior rate-cutting cycles.

Brazil's real policy rate is around 10%, among the highest globally, and local equities have an unusually strong inverse relationship with five-year Brazilian yields. The right-leaning policy basket (GSBZRIGH) has more exposure to banks, fintech, capital markets and long-duration equities.

Power Up America (GSENEPOW) is the preferred AI-related expression. Power supply, grid capacity and gas infrastructure remain constraints on datacenter buildout. GS estimates US data-center power demand could reach 108 GW by 2030, a 23% CAGR from the 2025 base, versus 3.5% CAGR for total US power demand.

The power complex has lagged other AI themes on affordability, permitting and regulatory concerns, but positioning and valuations have reset while equipment demand and construction activity remain robust. Catalysts: October 12 FERC decision on PJM's large-load framework, PJM reliability-backstop filings, Q3 results, December ERCOT interconnection audit.

Consumer Experiences (GSXUCEXP): spending growth on experiences accelerated from 1% in Q1 2025 to 6% in Q1 2026 versus 2% for broader services. The basket has underperformed the AI benchmark by 14% (a chart caption says ~16pp), with low relative valuations, improving earnings and ownership below prior peaks. Exposure skews to higher-income consumers.

Health care is the least correlated group to AI, oil and rates, with correlations closer to zero than negative, and strong positive earnings revisions, especially in commercial biotech (GSHLCOMB: N12m EPS growth 111%, YTD +25%).

Asia Battery Backup Units basket (GSXABBUS): GS estimates the global BBU market grows from $2.2B in 2025 to $50.2B by 2030 (87% CAGR), with attach rates near 95%. Panasonic is highlighted as a leading beneficiary on a 70-80% management-indicated global BBU share.

Systematic strategies: skew harvesting, macro vol selling (commodities, rates, credit, VIX), equity dispersion and select linear strategies such as commodity basis momentum and FX carry have outperformed YTD. Top Sharpe ratios include US Equity Daily Skew (4.34), CO Copper Volatility Carry (3.55) and EQ SPX Weekly VarSwap Carry (3.15).
